# ManaTuner — Product and Model Reference

Updated: 2026-09-06. This document describes the current source contracts; it does not certify a deployed configuration, legal compliance or all MTG interactions.

ManaTuner is a free, open-source Magic: The Gathering mana-base analyzer. It offers model-based probabilities, heuristic recommendations, opening-hand simulations, local history and a curated library.

URL: https://www.manatuner.app
Source: https://github.com/gbordes77/manatuner
License: MIT
Author: Guillaume Bordes

## Health Score

Health Score is a heuristic average of turn-two access to each required fixed color or hybrid alternative group. Physical sources are counted once within a hybrid union. It does not measure simultaneous payment of all pips, land sequencing or ramp. It is not the percentage of spells cast on curve, a win probability or a tournament-readiness certification.

Every format uses the same editorial bands:
- 85+ Excellent
- 70–84 Good
- 55–69 Average
- Below 55 Needs work

Unrepresented payment symbols can make the score unavailable. The UI and exports must preserve that state; an unavailable score is not a measured zero. Commander payment is shown separately; sideboard and command-zone cards do not contribute to the main-deck score.

## Castability and acceleration

The default is an estimate. The aggregate model approximates color access, land availability and acceleration. Mana rocks and dorks may contribute to that estimate; their inclusion does not make it exact.

Exact modes enumerate only their stated supported resource and sequencing model. Physical mana enumeration measures whether at least one legal sequence exists for a drawn history. This potential-castability event can overestimate the performance of a player who cannot foresee future draws. The separate payment-policy model uses a non-clairvoyant resource policy under its explicit assumptions. Neither is a complete gameplay or win-probability simulation.

Unsupported mechanics, missing required metadata and exhausted state budgets are reported rather than assigned a fabricated exact probability. Consult each model panel for supported sources, costs, target assumptions, turn range, removal and other exclusions. Conditional or restricted sources must be interpreted within that model's represented metadata.

Hypergeometric draw probabilities are exact for sampling without replacement:
P(X=k) = C(K,k) × C(N−K,n−k) / C(N,n).
N is library size, K desired cards, n cards drawn and k successes. Exact draw math does not establish exactness of an aggregate casting estimate.

Karsten source targets are reference comparisons, not a guarantee. Published rows depend on mana value, target reliability, mulligan and land-count assumptions. Scaling by N/60 outside published rows is approximate. Fixed-color targets and hybrid alternatives answer different questions; read the displayed limitations.

## Mulligan simulation

The standard setting uses 10,000 samples per kept-hand size, configurable up to 50,000. For each size from four to seven, the simulator shuffles the main deck, draws seven and selects a heuristic subset. In the London mulligan, each redraw is seven cards; after keeping, cards are put on the bottom for counted mulligans. Multiplayer mode models a free first mulligan and a turn-one draw.

Hand quality is a heuristic reward. Bellman backward induction computes stopping values for the sampled reward distributions, with a forced keep at four. The recursion is exact for those sampled distributions; estimated rewards and bottoming policy are not generally optimal gameplay. Plans use the displayed resource restrictions, including no ramp in the opening-hand plan model.

Sample-hand bands are 85+ Excellent, 70–84 Good, 55–69 Marginal, below 55 Poor. The separate deck-quality summary uses expected hand-quality value after modeled mulligans with bands 80/65/50. These describe different quantities from the deck-level Health Score.

Sampling uncertainty depends on the measured quantity and sample count. There is no universal ±1% accuracy guarantee for hand-quality scores, thresholds or model validity. The simulation does not play complete games or calculate win rate.

## Input populations and Commander

The parser supports explicit Deck, Sideboard, Commander, Maybeboard and Companion sections, inline SB prefixes and supported set/collector-number export syntax. Blank-line sideboard separation is a legacy heuristic with warnings, not universal format detection. Unparseable rows and input limits are reported before network resolution.

The main deck drives analysis. Sideboard remains separate for explicit post-board swaps. Maybeboard and Companion entries are excluded from card resolution and analysis with a warning. The input limit includes all zones.

Commander identification requires an explicit marker such as *CMDR* or a Commander section. An unmarked list does not acquire a commander from its first non-land card. Commander copies are excluded from the library; command-zone payment appears separately. Multiple commanders should be entered on separate lines in that section. Multiplayer politics and commander tax are outside the displayed castability model.

## Navigation, history and export

The five result tabs are Castability, Analysis, Mulligan, Manabase and Blueprint. PNG, PDF and JSON exports preserve the distinction between heuristic score, available model probability and unavailable result. Saved analyses stay in browser storage. History imports merge atomically by identifier; existing duplicates are kept, validation failures are reported, and storage failure must not silently discard history.

The library includes articles, podcasts, videos and references. Its current count is derived from articlesReferenceSeed in the application rather than duplicated here. Archived and lost sources are labeled; an HTTP 200 response alone does not certify the article content or access without a paywall.

## Network, storage and deletion

Calculations and saved analyses stay in this browser. No account is required. This is not a zero-transmission promise:
- Card lookups send names, identifiers or search terms to api.scryfall.com, including batches of names. These can reveal much of a deck; the saved analysis history is not uploaded by those lookups.
- Images use cards.scryfall.io. Google Fonts uses fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com; the mana-symbol font uses cdn.jsdelivr.net. Hosting and external services receive connection metadata such as IP and normal HTTP request information.
- Sentry initializes only in a production build with a configured DSN. The privacy page displays the build's monitoring condition. This static document does not certify deployed environment variables. No session replay is configured. Review actual event payloads, redaction, retention and applicable legal requirements before enabling monitoring; redaction is not a guarantee that arbitrary error text contains no sensitive data.

Saved analyses, current deck and preferences have no application expiry. Public card metadata in IndexedDB expires after 30 days; land metadata in local storage after 30 days; producer metadata after 7 days. Expiry is checked on use, not scheduled secure erasure. Session flags last for the browser session.

Reset requests removal of application local and session storage and starts asynchronous IndexedDB cleanup. Cleanup is best effort when storage is blocked. Reload to release in-memory caches; browser site-data controls offer broader local cleanup. Reset does not erase exported files, copied/shared links, browser history, third-party logs or copies on other devices.

Shared links encode the deck in the URL fragment; anyone with the link can recover it. Deleting local data does not revoke those copies. Legacy query-based links can disclose the payload to hosting logs. This technical inventory is not a declaration of legal compliance.

See https://www.manatuner.app/privacy for public information and docs/privacy/DATA-FLOWS.md in the repository for operator prerequisites.
